newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper, aluminium stocks tipped to fall-trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, aluminium stocks tipped to fall-trade.

text.p: Copper and aluminium stocks in the London Metal Exchange (LME) will probably fall later on Friday as the Chinese continued lifting small amounts of the red metal here, base metal dealers said.
Copper is seen falling 4,000-8,000 tonnes while aluminium will probably drop by 3,000-5,000 tonnes when the LME stocks report is released at 0800 GMT, the traders said.
"I think copper should be down about 4,000 tonnes," one dealer for a trading house in Singapore said.
Metal brokers Brandeis said copper inventories are "expected to fall by around 8,000 tonnes".
Traders said the Chinese, who have lifted large amounts of copper from the LME's Singapore warehouse, may buy only a small amount of about 500 to 1,000 tonnes.
Copper stocks in the LME warehouse in Singapore reached 38,825 tonnes last Tuesday, down 16,175 tonnes from the year's peak of 55,000 tonnes reported last March 14.
"I'd think most of the stuff went to China," one dealer for a European metal trading company said.
On aluminium, traders said stocks should slide by 3,000 to 5,000 tonnes although demand in the region has slowed down.
"Ally (aluminium) should be down 3,000-5,000 tonnes," one dealer said.
Three-month copper was quoted by regional dealers at 0200 GMT at around US$2,320/25 a tonne, barely changed from the late quote in London on Thursday of $2,320/25 a tonne.
Aluminium prices, on the other hand, were seen by the trade at 0200 GMT at $1,607/12 a tonne against the late trade in London yesterday of $1,607/10 a tonne.
